title: ECO Tiệm Số Hóa
tagline: Scaling a B2B2C merchant app that digitizes traditional grocery stores across Vietnam.

sections.heading: Context
sections.html: Traditional grocery stores (tạp hóa) are still the largest retail channel in Vietnam, but most of them run on paper and cash. FinViet's ECO Tiệm Số Hóa app connects these stores with FMCG manufacturers and adds payments and financial services on top: a manufacturer → merchant → consumer chain.

sections.heading: The problem
sections.html: The app already had 160K registered stores, but only about 20K used it in a given month. For the ecosystem to work, merchants needed a reason to open the app every day, and FMCG brands needed a reliable channel to reach them.

sections.heading: My role
sections.html: I owned the strategy and roadmap for the flagship merchant app and worked directly with C-level executives and business units to prioritize investments. I led delivery across BA, Engineering, Design, QA and Operations, and balanced requirements from FMCG partners such as KIDO, Tho Phat, Ajinomoto and Vifon.

list.title: Fix the daily workflows first
list.text: I mapped the core merchant workflows with BPMN, use case and sequence diagrams and redesigned them. Core tasks became 2.5x faster.

list.title: Bring existing financial services into the app
list.text: Instead of building new FinTech products, I integrated FinViet's existing e-wallet, QR payments, lending and bill pay into the merchant app, so a store could sell, collect payments and pay bills in one place.

list.title: Standard data flows for FMCG partners
list.text: I defined the integration data flows and API payload requirements so each brand could exchange orders and program data with the app securely.

list.title: Integrate AI rather than build it
list.text: I evaluated the trade-offs and integrated third-party computer vision and chatbot services to automate store operations and merchant support.

list.title: Give merchants reasons to come back
list.text: I delivered a Loyalty Portal (points earned on transactions, redeemable for vouchers) and a Gamification Portal that lets brands run in-app game campaigns.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.html:
• Registered users grew from 160K to 320K+ (2x).
  • Monthly active users grew from 20K to 90K+ (4.5x).
  • Retained merchants grew from 20K to 75K+ (3.75x).
  • Monthly transactions grew from 150K to 350K+ (2.3x).
  • Core merchant tasks became 2.5x faster.

title: UNA Market
tagline: Taking a Pinduoduo-style group-buying platform from concept to MVP.

sections.heading: Context
sections.html:
Fresh food in Vietnam passes through traders, wholesale markets and retail outlets before it reaches the shopper, and every step adds to the price. A tomato that leaves the farm at 7,000đ/kg can reach the shopper at 40,000đ/kg.

UNA Market tested a different model: shoppers team up to buy together, and the platform aggregates that demand to buy closer to the source.

sections.heading: The idea: interactive e-commerce
sections.html:
Classic e-commerce wins on convenience, efficiency and price, but loses the social and emotional side of shopping offline. The concept combined three things:

  • Recommendation: products find people, instead of people searching for products.
  • Entertainment: daily check-ins, price-chop and other game mechanics.
  • Community: shoppers invite friends and family to complete a team purchase.

sections.heading: My role
sections.html: I owned the product strategy and roadmap from 0 to 1: the business logic, product rules and functional specs for the web app and admin portal. I selected and managed the outsourced engineering vendor alongside the internal team, and owned the timeline, QA and final UAT sign-off.

list.title: Team purchase as the core loop
list.text: A shopper starts or joins a team, shares it on social networks, and the team has 24 hours to form. Every share brings in new users at low acquisition cost.

list.title: Dynamic tier pricing
list.text: I designed the group-buying rules and price tiers so the price drops as more people join, which gives every buyer a reason to invite others.

list.title: A lean MVP scope
list.text: The MVP covered the team-purchase flow, local payments, order processing and fulfillment. Growth mechanics were mapped to AARRR (pirate metrics) for later phases.

list.title: Outsource engineering, keep quality in-house
list.text: An external vendor built the product, while I kept control of quality through a QA framework and final UAT sign-off.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.html:
• Launched the MVP from concept.
  • Reached ~200M VND in monthly revenue within 8 months.

The group-buying experience from UNA carries directly into my current role, building a new group-buying platform at PIGROUP.

title: Haravan Omnichannel
tagline: POS and transaction modules for an omnichannel commerce platform serving 20K+ merchants.

sections.heading: Context
sections.html: Haravan is a B2B SaaS platform that lets retailers sell through physical stores, their own website, marketplaces and social channels from one system, with orders, inventory and customers in one place.

sections.heading: The problem
sections.html: In traditional retail, a merchant has to build and run separate systems for each sales channel, customer engagement, inventory, logistics and marketing. This takes a lot of resources and is hard to keep in sync. Large retail chains feel this the most at the point of sale, where every store and every channel has to see the same stock and the same orders.

sections.heading: My role
sections.html: I led the core POS and transaction modules for enterprise merchants. I translated store workflows into specs, user stories and acceptance criteria, prioritized the backlog, and worked with Engineering, QA, Sales and Customer Success through each sprint.

list.title: POS
list.text: In-store selling connected to the same product, order and customer data as the online channels.

list.title: Inventory
list.text: Stock that stays accurate across stores and channels.

list.title: Order & transaction management
list.text: One order flow from checkout to fulfillment, whichever channel the order came from.

list.title: Enterprise features
list.text: Features for retail chains including Vinamilk, The Coffee House and Juno.

sections.heading: How I prioritized
sections.html: I used merchant feedback and usage data to decide what to build next, focusing on the two things chains cared about most at the counter: checkout speed and inventory accuracy.

title: Cabina Live
tagline: A Chrome extension that adds a live transcript and real-time translation to Google Meet, with the translation read aloud in your headset.
role: Solo builder: product, design and AI-assisted development

sections.heading: The problem
sections.html:
Many engineers, PMs and designers now work remotely for overseas teams. In live meetings the language barrier is a daily source of stress:

  • Fear of missing what a manager or client just said.
  • Subtitles plus an AI voice on top of the original audio are tiring to follow.
  • Many companies block recording bots such as Otter.ai or Fireflies.ai from joining calls.
  • Most interpretation tools are monthly subscriptions whose minutes expire.

sections.heading: Research
sections.html: I compared the tools people actually use: Tactiq, JotMe, Wordly, Talo and Google Meet's own translation. Four gaps came up again and again in reviews: very broad extension permissions, high latency, bots that make people self-conscious, and opaque or expiring pricing.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.html:
Cabina Live adds a sidebar to the Google Meet call. It reads Meet's own live captions in the background, so Meet's CC button stays off and nothing changes for anyone else in the call. Lines are grouped by speaker, and each sentence is translated right under the original as soon as the speaker pauses. When Meet corrects a word, the line and its translation update.

The translation can also be read aloud in the user's headset, and "Original: Off" mutes the meeting audio while it plays, so the two voices never overlap. Every meeting can be reviewed and downloaded from the dashboard. The live transcript is free.

list.title: No bot, no recording
list.text: Reading Meet's captions instead of recording audio means nothing joins the call, it works where companies block bots, and no meeting audio is recorded or uploaded.

list.title: Permissions as a trust signal
list.text: Broad permissions were the top trust complaint about the closest competitor. Cabina asks only for Google Meet, sign-in and storage, and version 4.1 dropped even the activeTab permission.

list.title: Change the business model
list.text: Version 3 asked users to bring their own AI API key and buy a yearly license. The target users did not want to set up cloud keys, so version 4 moved to a free transcript plus prepaid translation hours with no subscription. Prepaid hours also cap the cost of each user at what they paid.

list.title: Manual language choice over auto-detect
list.text: Users pick the languages in the toolbar popup: Meet's 82 caption languages in, 190+ translation languages out. There is no auto-detect lag, so the first sentence is translated too.

list.title: Never translate the user's own lines
list.text: The user's own lines are transcribed but not translated or read back, so they cost nothing and do not clutter the headset.

sections.heading: Built with
sections.html: Chrome Extension (Manifest V3), Cloudflare Workers and D1 for accounts, prepaid hours and saved meetings, Google Cloud Translation and Text-to-Speech, and Polar for checkout. Built solo with AI-assisted development (Claude, Codex, Gemini).

title: UStillAlive
tagline: A safety app that lets family know you are OK without constant location tracking, and sends SOS alerts to a trusted circle.
role: Solo builder: product, design and AI-assisted development

sections.heading: The problem
sections.html: Most family safety apps track location in the background all the time. It drains the battery and feels like surveillance, so many people turn it off, and the app stops being useful when it matters.

list.title: Check-ins instead of tracking
list.text: The phone sends a light check-in signal. The trusted circle sees a simple status (Active, Warning or Inactive) instead of a live map.

list.title: Location only on SOS
list.text: GPS is used only when the user triggers an SOS. The alert includes the address, time and phone number.

list.title: A trusted circle
list.text: Alerts go to a small group of guardians the user chooses, and only they can see the data.

sections.heading: What I did
sections.html: I took the app from idea to both stores on my own: product definition, UX, AI-assisted development (Capacitor, Firebase, Cloud Functions, push notifications) and the App Store and Google Play releases.

title: PM No-Code
tagline: An online course on AI and no-code automation for product people who don't code, available on Udemy and Unica.

sections.heading: Who it is for
sections.html: Product managers, founders and operators without a coding background who want to automate their own work with AI and no-code tools, and understand how AI works well enough to work effectively with developers.

list.title: Product thinking for AI projects
list.text: Apply product management to AI and no-code projects, from the problem to the roadmap.

list.title: Workflow automation
list.text: Design and run automated workflows with modern no-code and low-code tools.

list.title: Prompt engineering and AI agents
list.text: Write structured prompts and build practical AI agent systems.

list.title: Real-world projects
list.text: Take a project from the first idea to a working system in daily use.

sections.heading: Course structure
sections.html: 92 lectures in Vietnamese (11 hours 40 minutes) across 8 modules: how AI works (machine learning, deep learning, LLMs), office AI with low-code automation and governance, AI agents and reasoning, MLOps and evaluation, and AI applications by industry.

sections.heading: How I produced it
sections.html: To produce 92 lectures on my own, I built a small automation tool for the studio work: converting slide decks, cleaning up recordings and splitting videos into lectures.

title: Dai-ichi Life App Platform
content_html:
Collaborated on the user experience and architecture of Dai-ichi Life's customer-facing mobile app, focusing on insurance data lookup and policy claim workflows.

Key UX contributions

  • Digital policy servicing: redesigned policy inquiry and claim submission flows to reduce paper and make self-service easier.
  • Customer journeys: streamlined the information architecture across policy overviews, premium payment schedules and claim status tracking.

title: PopsKids
content_html: Along with gaming, content for children is one of the top trends in Vietnam. With inappropriate content growing online, PopsKids was created as a safe space that filters out adult or sensitive media and shows only child-friendly programmes, across mobile and web.

title: PopsTV
content_html:
Designed the user interface flows for the PopsTV app, a multi-category video streaming service.

Design highlights

  • Content discovery: browsing categories, personalized watchlists and video playback controls.
  • Engagement: channel navigation and live-stream chat.

title: FoodSave App
content_html:
Singapore wastes about 788,600 tonnes of food a year, and only 13% is recycled. FoodSave is a concept app that connects food sellers and buyers (B2C and C2C) with real-time alerts on food that is about to expire.

Features

  • Merchant listings: merchants list products close to expiry and nearby users get discount alerts.
  • Peer-to-peer sharing: households can list extra cooked food or groceries before they expire.

title: Delivery Food App
content_html:
A concept food delivery app: browse local restaurants or search for a dish, see the delivery time and total price before ordering, and track the order in real time.

Features

  • Quick reordering and group ordering.
  • Scheduled deliveries.
  • Real-time tracking that factors in preparation time, traffic and weather.
  • No minimum order; pay by Google Pay or card.

title: 21 Academy – Blackjack Strategy Trainer
